story: Obatala, king of all the orishas and the oldest among them, was granted by the Supreme Deity the task of creating the Earth. Given a satchel of tools for creation, he was tempted by the trickster deity Eshu and became drunk on palm wine, failing in his task. His younger brother Oduduwa seized the satchel, used it to create land upon the primeval ocean, and was rewarded with the title "God of the Earth." Obatala was then given a new task: to create human beings. Assisted by Yemoo, he took a long gold chain, a snail's shell filled with sand, a white hen, a black cat, and a palm nut, and descended from Heaven on the chain. He released the white hen, which scattered the sand to form mountains and valleys, and planted the palm nut, which grew into a forest. Content with his work, he began molding humans from clay and water, but drank palm wine made from the forest he had created, growing drunk and shaping deformed figures. Upon sobering, he vowed never to drink again and to protect people with disabilities forever after. The finished humans were given a copper knife, a wooden hoe, and ase (life-force), and they prospered, with the Supreme Deity breathing life into them, making Obatala the father of humanity. In another telling, Obatala was a mortal king, founder and ruler of a great city. His rule was disrupted when Oduduwa led a usurpation against him. With the help of his supporters, Obatala overcame Oduduwa, caused his death, and retrieved his throne, ruling again as king.
blind: The hero, king of all divine beings and the oldest among them, was granted by the supreme creator the task of creating the Earth. Given a bag of tools for creation, he was tempted by a trickster spirit and became drunk on a fermented palm drink, failing in his task. His younger sibling seized the bag, used it to create land upon the primeval ocean, and was rewarded with the title "Ruler of the Earth." The hero was then given a new task: to create human beings. Assisted by a helper figure, he took a long metal chain, a snail's shell filled with sand, a white bird, a black animal, and a palm seed, and descended from the sky on the chain. He released the white bird, which scattered the sand to form mountains and valleys, and planted the seed, which grew into a forest. Content with his work, he began molding humans from clay and water, but drank a fermented drink made from the forest he had created, growing drunk and shaping deformed figures. Upon sobering, he vowed never to drink again and to protect people with disabilities forever after. The finished humans were given a metal blade, a farming tool, and a life-force, and they prospered, with the supreme creator breathing life into them, making the hero the father of humanity. In another telling, the hero was a mortal king, founder and ruler of a great city. His rule was disrupted when his rival led a usurpation against him. With the help of his supporters, the hero overcame his rival, caused his death, and retrieved his throne, ruling again as king.
